transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-09
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (EdenBridge), Ravi (EdenBridge), Sofia (EdenBridge), Tim (EdenBridge)

Auto-summary (auto): Discussed packaging checklist for marketplace listing, ref-arch cookbook steps, KMS/HSM questions, and UAT/benchmark plan. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Maya Chen: yeah, loud and clear. thanks alex. excited to dig in.
[00:12] Alex Martinez: perfect. quick intros — i'll run through the proposed ref-arch cookbook and packaging pattern, priya will go into the networking and perf checks, and liam will talk about the canary routing and fallback patterns for the listing.
[00:27] Priya Shah: hi hi — and i also have the sample helm values that we'll share, but we'll show a quick example of the operator flow too.
[00:34] Ravi Patel: quick note from our side — we're on AWS GovCloud for parts of this, and we need explicit KMS/HSM compatibility and govcloud packaging guidance.
[00:44] Alex Martinez: yes, noted. we'll call out the KMS variants — we have a compatibility matrix but i'll get the HSM notes from liam.
[00:52] Liam O'Neill: also want to flag quantization tradeoffs — if you go 4-bit int or q4 we can save tokens but latency may vary. we've seen a delta in throughput with small prompt sizes.
[01:08] Sofia Ruiz: can you expand on the delta? our product needs <120ms median for chat, but we also have cost constraints.
[01:16] Priya Shah: yeah so the thing is, small sequence lengths it's often better to keep some fp16 kernels; quant helps on throughput when you do batching but for tail latency you see more variance. that's where the smart routing + canary comes in.
[01:32] Maya Chen: we heard the word "smart routing" in the doc — is that something built into the Redwood listing or would we need to wire that in our gateway?
[01:39] Alex Martinez: good question. for the marketplace listing we recommend leaving routing to the Redwood runtime by default — you can opt into a hybrid mode where your gateway controls region affinity. we'll include code snippets in the cookbook.
[01:52] [01:52] Tim Waller: slight transcription note, my audio's a bit crunchy — but on KMS, we use Akeyless and also have a few HSM-backed keys from our provider. we need to know whether Redwood Private supports external HSM with bring-your-own-key.
[02:05] Liam O'Neill: yes, BYOK with HSM is supported in Private deployments, though there are a few operational steps and an HSM driver that must be installed. I'll add that to the matrix.
[02:18] Ravi Patel: and network — VPC peering vs private link — we prefer VPC peering, but if marketplace listing requires a connector, we need clear steps.
[02:27] Priya Shah: in the cookbook we'll show two patterns: 1) VPC peering with route table examples, 2) a connector pattern using PrivateLink-like interfaces and NAT. we'll also include firewall ports and helm value toggles.
[02:41] Maya Chen: can you show the helm sample now?
[02:44] Priya Shah: yeah, quick copy/paste — .. (screen share) .. values.yaml snippet: image.tag: "redwood-edge-1.3.2", networking.peering.enabled: true, kms.provider: "external", kms.secretRef: "redwood-kms-cred". forgive the auto transcript may write "secret ref" weirdly.
[03:06] Ravi Patel: that secretRef — are we expected to create a k8s secret or will the operator call out to KMS directly?
[03:12] Liam O'Neill: operator will lookup a secret only for bootstrap credentials, long term it exchanges with your KMS via the configured kms provider. full flow will be in the runbook.
[03:24] [03:24] Sofia Ruiz: what's the recommended deploy strategy for canary? we have multi-tenant traffic in prod.
[03:30] Alex Martinez: two-stage: first do a traffic-shift canary on the Redwood side with a 5-10% route to the new variant; second stage do a circuit-breaker fallback to a smaller model variant if latency or errors spike. we'll provide the route sample in canary.md.
[03:47] Priya Shah: realtime tracing hooks — add opentelemetry headers into requests so your observability picks up per-token latency. we have dashboards in Console tied to token-level cost.
[03:59] Tim Waller: security question — does the listing expose audit logs for customer-managed keys? we need attestable logs for SOC2.
[04:07] Alex Martinez: yes, audit logs are part of Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we provide tamper-evident logs with retention controls. we'll send SOC2 artifacts; note: sometimes the transcript spells it S-O-C two.
[04:22] Maya Chen: another constraint — we need to maintain data residency for EU customers; can the listing pin regional images to eu-west-1?
[04:30] Priya Shah: absolutely, the ref-arch cookbook will show region pinning and a policy for routing. we can also instrument failover to other regions but keep data residency controls enabled.
[04:43] Ravi Patel: about benchmarking — we want end-to-end p95 numbers with our prefix workload. how do we run that?
[04:50] Liam O'Neill: we'll run a small lab — priya will configure a UAT with your prompts and run both batched and non-batched cases, include KV cache warm-up. typical run takes 48 hours to stabilize.
[05:03] [05:03] Alex Martinez: quick pause — i'd like to call out packaging for the marketplace listing: you need an operator bundle, a helm chart, docs, and a verified image with digest. we've seen customers fail at digest pinning at the preflight stage.
[05:18] Sofia Ruiz: digest pinning — we use an internal registry proxy, can we use that?
[05:22] Priya Shah: yes, you can point the operator to your registry mirror, we'll include values for imagePullSecrets and registry mirrors in the cookbook.
[05:30] Tim Waller: about certs — mutual TLS between the connector and the Redwood runtime? we're required to have mTLS for cross-account links.
[05:38] Liam O'Neill: we support mTLS; the operator can bootstrap a cert pair and rotate via your cert manager. note, rotation requires the runtime to accept intermediate CA chains; we'll document that.
[05:51] Maya Chen: i'll be honest, our team is small — what's the expected ops effort to maintain a Private deployment vs using Hosted for the listing?
[05:59] Alex Martinez: Hosted is lowest ops, Dedicated is middle (we manage runtime but you get isolation), Private is highest ops but gives you full control and BYOK. for a listing we'd recommend starting Hosted or Dedicated and then plan Private for regulated customers.
[06:18] Ravi Patel: cost — do you have an estimate template in the cookbook?
[06:22] Priya Shah: yes we'll include a cost-model sheet: tokens per request, batching multipliers, GPU hour estimates per qps, and quantization uplift numbers. we'll share a spreadsheet.
[06:34] Sofia Ruiz: competitor question — we've seen CloudWave's connector that bundles a sidecar; how is your operator different?
[06:41] Alex Martinez: our operator focuses on runtime-aware optimizations: KV cache lifecycle, seamless rollouts with model variants, and built-in prefix caching. plus first-class Console observability. sometimes the auto transcript calls it "K-V cash life cycle" which is funny.
[06:58] Priya Shah: also we try to avoid heavy sidecars — prefer controller + minimal daemonset.
[07:07] Maya Chen: timeline — we ideally want a pilot within 3 weeks and production listing in 8 weeks. possible?
[07:13] Alex Martinez: yes, that's doable: week 1 packaging + checklist, week 2 UAT and lab runs, week 3 quantization pilot, weeks 4-8 address feedback and marketplace preflight.
[07:26] [07:26] Tim Waller: about preflight — what's in the preflight gate? network, image digest, RBAC, helm values, and telemetry?
[07:34] Liam O'Neill: correct. and we'll run an automated smoke test that hits the runtime and validates a sample prompt set. we also check kms access patterns.
[07:46] Ravi Patel: any gotchas with GovCloud? we've had endpoints blocked before.
[07:50] Priya Shah: GovCloud needs explicit endpoint allow-lists and for some HSM vendors you need extra VPC endpoints. we'll include a GovCloud appendix.
[08:01] Sofia Ruiz: can we get a small checklist for compliance review for the marketplace?
[08:05] Alex Martinez: yes — checklist includes SOC artifacts, SAML/SSO config, KMS attestation, encryption in transit + at rest, and data residency declarations. we'll attach that.
[08:17] Priya Shah: quick demo note — when you run the UAT we'll collect p50/p95/p99 with and without KV cache warm. that shows real benefits of prefix caching.
[08:30] Maya Chen: does Redwood support prefix caching for multi-tenant mode? our tenants share prompts.
[08:36] Liam O'Neill: yes but with tenant isolation — KV cache keys are namespaced per customer by default. you can configure cross-tenant shared caches but we warn about leakage.
[08:48] Ravi Patel: on the operator upgrade path — can we do zero-downtime model version swaps?
[08:54] Priya Shah: yes, the runtime supports in-place KV cache hydration and smooth switchovers if you follow the rollout pattern in the runbook. we'll include a pre/post checklist.
[09:05] [09:05] Alex Martinez: ok i'd like to surface two deeper follow-ups: 1) a lab for quantization perf with your prefix set, 2) an HSM compatibility spike with your vendor. priya and liam will own.
[09:15] Maya Chen: sounds good.
[09:18] Tim Waller: small point — we use SAML SSO via our IdP, any gotchas?
[09:22] Liam O'Neill: we support SAML and OIDC; for marketplace listing we provide a metadata sample and attribute mapping. sometimes the transcript writes Id-P as "eye-dee pee".
[09:32] Sofia Ruiz: ok next, can you enumerate files we'll get after this call?
[09:36] Alex Martinez: sure — packaging checklist + Helm values, ref-arch cookbook draft, KMS/HSM matrix, lab runbook and benchmark plan, SOC2 artifacts bundle, and a proposed timeline. you'll get a link to a shared drive.
[09:55] Priya Shah: i'll post the helm values and a minimal sample repo during the day.
[10:01] Maya Chen: awesome. one more technical — how do you handle large context windows? we may need 64k windows for some customers.
[10:09] Liam O'Neill: runtime supports up to 128k in certain model builds, but there are kernel tradeoffs. the cookbook will call out kernel tuning and memory footprint per sequence length.
[10:24] Ravi Patel: may we run a 24-hour soak test on your dedicated infra?
[10:28] Alex Martinez: yes, we do a 24-48 hour soak for pilots. we'll allocate dedicated capacity for your pilot if needed.
[10:36] [10:36] Sofia Ruiz: timeline recap?
[10:38] Alex Martinez: send checklist today, run UAT week of 8/16, quant pilot week of 8/23, KMS spike by 8/13, and marketplace preflight in early Sept.
[10:52] Maya Chen: ok thanks we'll review.
[10:55] Priya Shah: one last note — please share your sample prompt set, that's critical for the benchmark.
[11:01] Ravi Patel: will do.
[11:03] Alex Martinez: great — i'll follow up with the package and links. thanks all.
[11:08] End of recording.
